launch.command: Every command of this freeze, whatever its phase, runs as its 'shell' member alone. The Director replaces only the named placeholders (its deferred_arguments), each by its 64-hex value taken mechanically from the frozen source; they sit inside single quotes, and the values hold no quote. Nothing is prepended or appended, so that zsh -c runs one simple command and the wrapper leads its group. The string goes to the shell tool in background mode, with no tool timeout: one call per command, never retried.
launch.timer: In the same message, the Director passes the command's 'timer_shell' member, read the same way and passed alone, to the shell tool, also in background mode with no tool timeout. It is 'timer_template' with the command's exit file (records.exit) and its limits.outer_bound_s. It exits at the first of two events: the exit file exists, or more than outer_bound_s seconds have passed since it began. It prints which: 'bound-timer: exit-file ...' with status 0, or 'bound-timer: outer-bound ...' with status 1, each with its start and current epoch seconds. It starts only shell builtins (and forks of its own shell for $(...)), /bin/date and /bin/sleep, and writes nothing.
launch.timer_template:
f='{exit_file}'; b={bound}; s=$(/bin/date +%s); case $s in ''|*[!0-9]*) printf 'bound-timer: no-clock file=%s
' "$f"; exit 2;; esac; while :; do if [ -e "$f" ]; then printf 'bound-timer: exit-file began=%s now=%s bound_s=%s file=%s
' "$s" "$(/bin/date +%s)" "$b" "$f"; exit 0; fi; n=$(/bin/date +%s); case $n in ''|*[!0-9]*) printf 'bound-timer: no-clock file=%s
' "$f"; exit 2;; esac; if [ "$n" -gt "$((s + b))" ]; then printf 'bound-timer: outer-bound began=%s now=%s bound_s=%s file=%s
' "$s" "$n" "$b" "$f"; exit 1; fi; /bin/sleep 1; done
launch.after: The Director goes on when the command's background task has ended and its timer has printed 'exit-file'. 'outer-bound' while the command's task is still running: the overrun rule ('overrun'). 'no-clock', or any other output or status of a timer: a PLAN deviation of this freeze's own tool; the Director records it, waits for the command's task without a bound, runs the command's .L, .P and .X as frozen, and stops S7 after them. A timer line printed after the command's task ended (a wrapper exit 90, 91 or 92 leaves no exit file) is recorded and has no effect.
launch.p00: P00's outcome is read from its wrapper's exit file alone (FR-07; stop rule 1).
launch.starts: The Director's, recorded and not bounded: one zsh per tool call (a command, a timer, a selection); each timer's /bin/date once at its start, about once a second and once at exit-file, and its /bin/sleep about once a second; one jq per member read.
